Public blog revision · 11 September 2026

This revision rewrites the explanatory paragraphs across all 50 lessons after reading the main manuscript and its appendices. The talk follows the hidden scalar through point addition, arithmetic, scheduling, protected measurements, and factory supply. Each construction is introduced through the operation it needs to perform before its notation and resource accounting.

The figures, tables, interactive visuals, and displayed equations are retained. The revision record lists the page coverage and verification. Stable section anchors and the public project prefix keep existing deep links and data references usable.

Earlier section-by-section coverage record

Section-by-section context audit

The earlier context audit established the lesson inventory and added local explanations of inputs, domains, widths, and measurement outcomes. Its drawings cover lookup cleanup, phase-sensitive readout, compiler decomposition, detector connectivity, carry escape, independent factory inputs, and phase estimation.

That earlier work is recorded below as provenance. The current narration develops the mechanism around those preserved visual objects. Exact tables continue to supply mappings and numerical values where the reader needs to compare individual entries.

The audit separates what the website checks directly from results imported from the paper. This distinction applies equally to its own statements about verification.

The earlier machine-readable record describes its algebraic and structural checks. The current revision record separately reports the new prose and rendered-site review.

Three kinds of evidence

EvidenceWhat these notes establish
Algebra and disclosed circuitsCheck identities, phase conventions, and finite input domains.
Compiler and decoder resultsExplain the published schedule and simulation settings.
Heuristic and hardware assumptionsState the conditions used by the end-to-end estimate.

Checks with mathematical consequences

The retained checks cover arithmetic replay, signed gcd updates, temporary ANDs, history compression, Fourier conventions, the linear amplitude correction, and accepted distillation errors. They also include 512 CCZ data/outcome assignments, 190 Q66 representative records, and 120 single two-qubit encoder faults. These are checks of the exposed constructions and examples.

Details that change interpretation

Source quantityHow to read it
≈39 million / 40,420,330 ToffolisDifferent counting conventions; the second is the compiled injection count.
29.50 ms per layerRounded. Appendix E23 gives 29.4958 ms, reproducing 25.690 days.
40.7% conservative branchRequires recovery search covering the omitted-window ambiguity, and modeled hardware reliability.
26.46% hardware failureCombines categories as independent. Their union bound is about 27.44%.

Two distinctions affect the numerical interpretation. Appendix B transfers field-input failure counts to curve inputs using multiplicities. The Eastin lesson distinguishes the leading quadratic term from the exact error conditioned on acceptance.

The inventory retains every numbered main section, all seven appendices, and 22 essential reference constructions. Each dedicated page explains its role in the same end-to-end calculation.

Diagrams and data

The original circuits and routing figures remain at full resolution, including both parts of Figure 21. The runtime chart is computed from disclosed table values. Figures 7 and 22 retain their source-PDF provenance because point-by-point simulation samples are not supplied.

Scope of verification

The authors' internal compiler and full noise simulations have not been rerun here. The website's checks cover exposed mathematical examples, generated math, links, assets, and targets; its Fourier controls are compared with the exact inverse transform for all 49 settings. The evidence ledger records sources, and Limitations collects the remaining scientific and reproduction gaps.
